domain: Cal/OSHA safety program obligations for California construction employers: IIPP (8 CCR 3203/1509), Code of Safe Practices and toolbox meetings, outdoor and indoor heat illness (3395/3396), serious injury reporting (342/330), Log 300 recordkeeping and OSHA electronic submission (14300 series), Cal/OSHA permits (341 series), asbestos registration/certification (341.6-341.12, 1529, B&P 7058.5 etc.), lead (1532.1), respirable silica (1532.3), fall protection and fall protection plans (1670, 1671.1, 1716.2, 1730, 1731), excavation (1541/1541.1), first aid/EMS and sanitation (1512, 1526, 1527), cranes (5021, 5006.2), falsework/scaffolds (1717, 1637), HazCom and respirators (5194, 5144), Workplace Violence Prevention Plans (Labor Code 6401.9), and Cal/OSHA and CSLB penalties
source_doc: Official Title 8 CCR section pages fetched and read from dir.ca.gov (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/<section>.html and https://www.dir.ca.gov/T8/14300_xx.html, including Appendices H and I to 14300.48), fetched 2026-11-25; official Cal/OSHA workplace violence pages (General-Industry.html, FAQ.html, Laws-in-General-Industry.html), Cal/OSHA Model WVPP (.docx), DIR May 13 2025 draft-vs-LC 6401.9 comparison (.docx) and DIR WVP rulemaking page; and the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt, PDF pages 45-49, 84-86, 246, 274-275, 346, 351, 356-357, 465-466, 540). leginfo.legislature.ca.gov (Labor Code statute text, e.g., 6401.9, 6500-6510, 6425 fine amounts) was NOT reachable (403/DNS-blocked), so Labor Code items rely on DIR/CSLB official restatements and are flagged in notes. The Law Book itself contains little Cal/OSHA program content: injury reporting (LC 6409.1), posting (LC 6408), LC 6425, B&P 7109.5/7110 discipline, and asbestos certification/registration (B&P 7058.5, 7058.6, 7028.1, 7099.11, 7118.4, 7118.5; 16 CCR 832.22).

rules.title: Written Injury and Illness Prevention Program (IIPP) required
rules.plain_english: Every employer must have a written IIPP that is actually implemented and kept up to date. Construction employers are required to have one by Construction Safety Order 1509, which points to the general IIPP rule in section 3203.
rules.applies_to: All California employers with employees on construction jobsites (every employer; no size exemption from having a program)
rules.verbatim_quote: Effective July 1, 1991, every employer shall establish, implement and maintain an effective Injury and Illness Prevention Program (Program). The Program shall be in writing and, shall, at a minimum:
rules.notes: Element (a)(8) employee access was added effective 2020-07-01. 8 CCR 1509(a) separately requires construction employers to maintain an IIPP 'in accordance with section 3203'. A Workplace Violence Prevention Plan may be a separate section of the IIPP (Labor Code 6401.9).

rules.title: Construction employers: IIPP under CSO 1509
rules.plain_english: The Construction Safety Orders independently require every construction employer to establish, implement and maintain an effective IIPP following section 3203.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers
rules.verbatim_quote: (a) Every employer shall establish, implement and maintain an effective Injury and Illness Prevention Program in accordance with section 3203 of the General Industry Safety Orders.

rules.title: IIPP hazard inspections: when they must happen
rules.plain_english: Your IIPP must include scheduled periodic inspections, and inspections are also required when the program is first set up, when new substances, processes, procedures or equipment bring new hazards, and whenever you learn of a new or previously unrecognized hazard.
rules.applies_to: All California employers with employees on construction jobsites
rules.verbatim_quote: Include procedures for identifying and evaluating work place hazards including scheduled periodic inspections to identify unsafe conditions and work practices.
rules.notes: The regulation does not fix a numeric inspection interval; the frequency is set by the employer's program. Tool can schedule recurring jobsite inspections and log them (see iipp-inspection-records-1-year).

rules.title: IIPP: correct hazards in a timely manner; remove workers from imminent hazards
rules.plain_english: Unsafe conditions must be corrected in a timely manner based on severity. If an imminent hazard can't be fixed right away, everyone except the people needed to correct it must be removed from the area.
rules.applies_to: All California employers with employees on construction jobsites
rules.verbatim_quote: When an imminent hazard exists which cannot be immediately abated without endangering employee(s) and/or property, remove all exposed personnel from the area except those necessary to correct the existing condition.

rules.title: IIPP training: when it must be given
rules.plain_english: Safety training must be given when the program starts, to every new employee, to employees given new assignments, when new substances/processes/equipment introduce new hazards, when new hazards are recognized, and to supervisors on the hazards their crews face.
rules.applies_to: All California employers with employees on construction jobsites
rules.verbatim_quote: (B) To all new employees; (C) To all employees given new job assignments for which training has not previously been received;

rules.title: Employers with fewer than 10 employees may communicate safety orally
rules.plain_english: If you have fewer than 10 employees, you may meet the IIPP communication requirement by instructing employees orally on general safe work practices and job-specific hazards.
rules.applies_to: Employers with fewer than 10 employees
rules.verbatim_quote: Exception: Employers having fewer than 10 employees shall be permitted to communicate to and instruct employees orally in general safe work practices with specific instructions with respect to hazards unique to the employees' job assignments as compliance with subsection (a)(3).
rules.notes: The program itself must still be in writing; this exception only relaxes the communication element.

rules.title: Give employees a copy of the IIPP within 5 business days
rules.plain_english: When an employee or their designated representative asks for the IIPP, you must provide access no later than 5 business days after the request. The first printed copy is free.

parameters.trigger: request from employee or designated representative
parameters.format_default: printed unless requester agrees to electronic
parameters.alternative: unobstructed electronic access via company server/website

rules.applies_to: All California employers with employees on construction jobsites
rules.verbatim_quote: Provide access in a reasonable time, place, and manner, but in no event later than five (5) business days after the request for access is received from an employee or designated representative.
rules.notes: Additional copies within 1 year with no updates may carry reasonable reproduction cost. Records of implementation steps need not be included.

rules.title: Keep IIPP inspection records at least 1 year
rules.plain_english: Records of scheduled and periodic inspections (who inspected, what was found, what was done to fix it) must be kept at least one year.
rules.applies_to: All California employers with employees on construction jobsites
rules.verbatim_quote: These records shall be maintained for at least one (1) year; and Exception: Employers with fewer than 10 employees may elect to maintain the inspection records only until the hazard is corrected.

rules.title: Keep safety training records at least 1 year
rules.plain_english: Document each employee's safety training (name or ID, dates, type of training, trainer) and keep it at least one year.

parameters.lt_10_employees_alternative: log of instructions given at hire/new duties
parameters.short_tenure_exception: employees with < 1 year may receive records at termination instead

rules.applies_to: All California employers with employees on construction jobsites
rules.verbatim_quote: Documentation of safety and health training required by subsection (a)(7) for each employee, including employee name or other identifier, training dates, type(s) of training, and training providers. This documentation shall be maintained for at least one (1) year.
rules.notes: Note 2 to 3203: CSLB-licensed construction employers may use training records from a Division-approved OSH training program and need only keep records of program steps for hazards specific to the employee's job duties.

rules.title: Reduced IIPP documentation for some employers under 20 employees
rules.plain_english: Employers with fewer than 20 employees that are not on DIR's high-hazard list and have an experience modification rate (EMR) of 1.1 or less may limit written IIPP documentation to: the responsible person, periodic inspections, and training.

parameters.condition: industry not on DIR designated high-hazard list (or industry on DIR low-hazard list)

rules.applies_to: Small employers not in designated high-hazard industries
rules.verbatim_quote: For Employers with fewer than 20 employees who are in industries that are not on a designated list of high-hazard industries established by the Department of Industrial Relations (Department) and who have a Workers' Compensation Experience Modification Rate of 1.1 or less
rules.notes: Many construction trades appear on DIR's high-hazard industry list, which would make this exception unavailable; the list itself was not reviewed here. Treat as 'check eligibility' rather than auto-apply.

rules.title: Labor/management safety committee option: meet at least quarterly
rules.plain_english: If you use a labor/management safety committee to satisfy IIPP communication, it must meet at least quarterly and keep written meeting records for at least one year.
rules.applies_to: Employers that elect a labor/management safety and health committee
rules.verbatim_quote: (1) Meets regularly, but not less than quarterly;

rules.title: Written Code of Safe Practices required
rules.plain_english: Every construction employer must adopt a written Code of Safe Practices specific to its operations, using language equivalent to the relevant parts of Plate A-3 in the Construction Safety Orders appendix.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers
rules.verbatim_quote: (b) Every employer shall adopt a written Code of Safe Practices which relates to the employer's operations. The Code shall contain language equivalent to the relevant parts of Plate A-3 of the Appendix.

rules.title: Post the Code of Safe Practices at each jobsite office
rules.plain_english: Post the Code of Safe Practices in a conspicuous place at each jobsite office, or give a copy to every supervisor to keep readily available.

parameters.posting_location: conspicuous location at each job site office
parameters.alternative: provided to each supervisory employee, readily available

rules.applies_to: Construction employers, each jobsite
rules.verbatim_quote: (c) The Code of Safe Practices shall be posted at a conspicuous location at each job site office or be provided to each supervisory employee who shall have it readily available.

rules.title: Periodic management-led supervisor safety meetings
rules.plain_english: Management must hold periodic meetings of supervisors to discuss safety problems and accidents that have occurred.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers
rules.verbatim_quote: (d) Periodic meetings of supervisory employees shall be held under the direction of management for the discussion of safety problems and accidents that have occurred.

rules.title: Toolbox/tailgate safety meetings at least every 10 working days
rules.plain_english: Supervisors must hold a toolbox or tailgate safety meeting (or equivalent) with their crews at least every 10 working days.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers, every crew
rules.verbatim_quote: (e) Supervisory employees shall conduct "toolbox" or "tailgate" safety meetings, or equivalent, with their crews at least every 10 working days to emphasize safety.
rules.notes: 1509 itself does not set a sign-in sheet requirement; documenting attendance supports 3203(b)(2) training records. Interval counts working days, not calendar days.

rules.title: Instruct new workers and have them read the Code of Safe Practices
rules.plain_english: When workers are first employed they must be instructed on the hazards and precautions for their type of work and directed to read the Code of Safe Practices. Workers exposed to known site hazards (chemicals, confined spaces, etc.) must be trained on recognizing the hazard, protection, and first aid.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers
rules.verbatim_quote: (a) When workers are first employed they shall be given instructions regarding the hazards and safety precautions applicable to the type of work in question and directed to read the Code of Safe Practices.

rules.title: Only qualified persons may operate equipment
rules.plain_english: Only qualified persons may be allowed to operate equipment and machinery.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers
rules.verbatim_quote: (b) The employer shall permit only qualified persons to operate equipment and machinery.

rules.title: Survey the site for hazards before employees arrive
rules.plain_english: Before your employees are on site, survey site conditions to identify predictable hazards and the safeguards needed. No worker may be required to work in an unsafe place except to make it safe with precautions.

parameters.timing: prior to presence of employees on site
parameters.reference: CSO Appendix Plate A-2-a and b

rules.applies_to: Construction employers, each new jobsite
rules.verbatim_quote: (b) Prior to the presence of its employees, the employer shall make a thorough survey of the conditions of the site to determine, so far as practicable, the predictable hazards to employees and the kind and extent of safeguards necessary to prosecute the work in a safe manner

rules.title: Definition: Competent Person (Construction Safety Orders)
rules.plain_english: A competent person can identify existing and predictable hazards and has authority to take prompt corrective action. Many rules (excavations, scaffolds, silica, asbestos, fall protection plans) require one to be designated.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers
rules.verbatim_quote: Competent Person. One who is capable of identifying existing and predictable hazards in the surroundings or working conditions which are unsanitary, hazardous, or dangerous to employees, and who has authorization to take prompt corrective measures to eliminate them.

rules.title: Definition: Qualified Person (Construction Safety Orders)
rules.plain_english: A qualified person is someone the employer designates who, by training, experience or instruction, has shown they can safely perform the assigned duties and holds any required license.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers
rules.verbatim_quote: Qualified Person, Attendant or Operator. A person designated by the employer who by reason of training, experience or instruction has demonstrated the ability to safely perform all assigned duties and, when required, is properly licensed in accordance with federal, state, or local laws and regulations.

rules.title: Outdoor heat standard applies to construction, including high-heat procedures
rules.plain_english: The outdoor heat illness standard covers all outdoor workplaces; construction is one of the listed industries that must also follow the high-heat (95F) procedures.

parameters.standard_name: Maria Isabel Vasquez Jimenez heat illness standard
industries_subject_to_high_heat_subsecti: transportation/delivery of agricultural products, construction materials or other heavy materials

rules.applies_to: Construction employers with employees working outdoors
rules.verbatim_quote: (2) List of industries subject to all provisions of this standard, including subsection (e): (A) Agriculture (B) Construction

rules.title: Provide 1 quart of drinking water per employee per hour
rules.plain_english: Provide fresh, pure, suitably cool water free of charge, as close as practicable to the work. If water isn't plumbed, bring enough at the start of the shift for 1 quart per employee per hour for the whole shift (or have effective refill procedures).

parameters.location: as close as practicable to work areas
parameters.calc: quarts_at_shift_start = employees * shift_hours (unless effective replenishment procedures)

rules.applies_to: Construction employers with employees working outdoors
rules.verbatim_quote: Where drinking water is not plumbed or otherwise continuously supplied, it shall be provided in sufficient quantity at the beginning of the work shift to provide one quart per employee per hour for drinking for the entire shift.
rules.notes: 4 cups/hour figure is from the training topic in 3395(h)(1)(C). Example: 8 workers x 10-hour shift = 80 quarts (20 gallons).

rules.title: Shade must be up when temperature exceeds 80F
rules.plain_english: When the outdoor temperature in the work area exceeds 80F, keep shade set up at all times while employees are present, big enough for everyone on rest or recovery periods to sit fully in the shade without touching. At 80F or below, provide shade or timely access on request.

parameters.shade_capacity: all employees on recovery/rest periods seated in normal posture without contact
parameters.meal_period_capacity: employees on meal period who remain onsite
parameters.at_or_below_80f: provide shade or timely access on request
parameters.temperature_measurement: dry bulb, in full sun with sensor shielded

rules.applies_to: Construction employers with employees working outdoors
rules.verbatim_quote: (1) Shade shall be present when the temperature exceeds 80 degrees Fahrenheit. When the outdoor temperature in the work area exceeds 80 degrees Fahrenheit, the employer shall have and maintain one or more areas with shade at all times while employees are present that are either open to the air or provided with ventilation or cooling.
rules.notes: Exceptions: alternative procedures if shade structure infeasible/unsafe; non-agriculture employers may use equally effective cooling measures (e.g., misters).

rules.title: Preventative cool-down rest: at least 5 minutes, monitored
rules.plain_english: Employees may take a cool-down rest in the shade whenever they need it. The employee must be monitored, asked about symptoms, encouraged to stay in shade, and not ordered back until symptoms are gone and at least 5 minutes have passed (plus time to reach the shade).

parameters.allowed: at all times on employee request

rules.applies_to: Construction employers with employees working outdoors
rules.verbatim_quote: (C) shall not be ordered back to work until any signs or symptoms of heat illness have abated, but in no event less than 5 minutes in addition to the time needed to access the shade.

rules.title: High-heat procedures at 95F and above
rules.plain_english: When the temperature is 95F or higher, construction employers must: keep effective communication to a supervisor, observe employees (one supervisor/designee per 20 or fewer, a buddy system, or regular contact with solo workers), designate someone to call EMS, remind workers to drink water throughout the shift, and hold pre-shift meetings on high-heat procedures.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers with employees working outdoors (construction is a listed high-heat industry)
rules.verbatim_quote: (e) High-heat procedures. The employer shall implement high-heat procedures when the temperature equals or exceeds 95 degrees Fahrenheit.
rules.notes: The mandatory 10-minute-every-2-hours cool-down at 95F in (e)(6) applies only to agriculture, not construction.

rules.title: Pre-shift heat meeting on 95F days
rules.plain_english: On high-heat days, hold a meeting before work starts to review high-heat procedures, encourage drinking water, and remind workers of their right to take cool-down rests.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers with employees working outdoors
rules.verbatim_quote: (5) Pre-shift meetings before the commencement of work to review the high heat procedures, encourage employees to drink plenty of water, and remind employees of their right to take a cool-down rest when necessary.

rules.title: Heat emergency response procedures
rules.plain_english: Have working communication to reach a supervisor or EMS, respond immediately to heat illness signs, never leave a symptomatic worker alone or send them home without offering first aid/EMS, and be able to give clear directions to the site.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers with employees working outdoors
rules.verbatim_quote: (C) An employee exhibiting signs or symptoms of heat illness shall be monitored and shall not be left alone or sent home without being offered onsite first aid and/or being provided with emergency medical services in accordance with the employer's procedures.

rules.title: Close observation: heat waves and new workers' first 14 days
rules.plain_english: Closely observe all employees during a heat wave (forecast high at least 80F and at least 10F above the prior 5-day average high), and closely observe any employee newly assigned to a high-heat area for their first 14 days.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers with employees working outdoors
rules.verbatim_quote: For purposes of this section only, “heat wave” means any day in which the predicted high temperature for the day will be at least 80 degrees Fahrenheit and at least ten degrees Fahrenheit higher than the average high daily temperature in the preceding five days.

rules.title: Heat illness training before work in heat
rules.plain_english: Every employee and supervisor must be trained on heat illness before starting work where heat exposure is reasonably anticipated. Supervisors also need training on implementing procedures, responding to symptoms, and monitoring weather.

parameters.timing: before employee begins work reasonably anticipated to expose to heat illness risk

rules.applies_to: Construction employers with employees working outdoors
rules.verbatim_quote: Effective training in the following topics shall be provided to each supervisory and non-supervisory employee before the employee begins work that should reasonably be anticipated to result in exposure to the risk of heat illness:

rules.title: Written Heat Illness Prevention Plan (English + majority language)
rules.plain_english: Have a written Heat Illness Prevention Plan in English and in the language understood by most of your employees, available at the worksite. It must cover water and shade, high-heat procedures, emergency response, and acclimatization. It may be part of the IIPP.

languages: language understood by majority of employees

rules.applies_to: Construction employers with employees working outdoors
rules.verbatim_quote: The plan shall be in writing in both English and the language understood by the majority of the employees and shall be made available at the worksite to employees and to representatives of the Division upon request.

rules.title: Indoor heat standard applies at 82F; full controls at 87F
rules.plain_english: The indoor heat rule applies to indoor work areas at or above 82F while employees are present. The full assessment and control requirements apply if the temperature or heat index reaches 87F, or 82F where workers wear heat-restrictive clothing or work near high radiant heat.
rules.applies_to: Employers with indoor work areas at or above 82F (includes indoor construction work areas)
rules.verbatim_quote: (1) This section applies to all indoor work areas where the temperature equals or exceeds 82 degrees Fahrenheit when employees are present.
rules.notes: 'Indoor' means under a ceiling/overhead covering AND enclosed along the entire perimeter by walls/windows/etc. (open or closed). Partially enclosed construction areas may instead fall under 3395. Incidental exception does not apply to vehicles without working A/C.

rules.title: Indoor cool-down area kept below 82F
rules.plain_english: Keep one or more cool-down areas available whenever employees are present, large enough for those on breaks, and keep indoor cool-down areas below 82F unless infeasible. Cool-down rests: at least 5 minutes plus access time.
rules.applies_to: Employers with indoor work areas at or above 82F (includes indoor construction work areas)
rules.verbatim_quote: The temperature in indoor cool-down areas shall be maintained at less than 82 degrees Fahrenheit, unless the employer demonstrates it is infeasible.

rules.title: Indoor heat: measure, record, retain 12 months
rules.plain_english: Where the full indoor heat rule applies, measure temperature and heat index, record whichever is greater with date, time and location, re-measure when readings are expected to be 10F or more higher, and keep records 12 months or until the next measurement, whichever is later.

parameters.record_value: greater of temperature or heat index
parameters.retention_rule: 12 months or until next measurements, whichever later

rules.applies_to: Employers with indoor work areas at or above 82F (includes indoor construction work areas)
rules.verbatim_quote: 3. Records, as required by subsection (e)(1)(A), shall be retained for 12 months or until the next measurements are taken, whichever is later.

rules.title: Indoor heat control measures (engineering first)
rules.plain_english: Use engineering controls to keep temperature and heat index below 87F (below 82F for heat-restrictive clothing or high radiant heat) unless infeasible, then administrative controls, then personal heat-protective equipment.
rules.applies_to: Employers with indoor work areas at or above 82F (includes indoor construction work areas)
rules.verbatim_quote: (A) Engineering controls. Engineering controls shall be used to reduce and maintain both the temperature and heat index to below 87 degrees Fahrenheit when employees are present,

rules.title: Indoor heat: observe new workers 14 days
rules.plain_english: Closely observe employees newly assigned to indoor areas at 87F+ (temperature or heat index), or 82F+ with restrictive clothing or high radiant heat, for their first 14 days; and all employees during a heat wave if no engineering controls offset outdoor heat.
rules.applies_to: Employers with indoor work areas at or above 82F (includes indoor construction work areas)
rules.verbatim_quote: (2) An employee who has been newly assigned to any of the following shall be closely observed by a supervisor or designee for the first 14 days of employment:

rules.title: Written indoor Heat Illness Prevention Plan
rules.plain_english: Have a written indoor heat plan in English and the majority language, available at the worksite, covering water, cool-down areas, measurement and controls, emergency response, and acclimatization. It may be combined with the IIPP or the outdoor heat plan.

languages: language understood by majority of employees

rules.applies_to: Employers with indoor work areas at or above 82F (includes indoor construction work areas)
rules.verbatim_quote: The Heat Illness Prevention Plan may be included as part of the employer's Injury and Illness Prevention Program required by section 3203 or Heat Illness Prevention Plan required by section 3395

rules.title: Report serious injury, illness or death to Cal/OSHA within 8 hours
rules.plain_english: Report any employee death or serious injury/illness to Cal/OSHA immediately: as soon as practically possible but no later than 8 hours after you knew or should have known. Up to 24 hours only if you can show exigent circumstances. Report by phone or the Division's online mechanism.

parameters.clock_starts: when employer knows or with diligent inquiry would have known
methods: Division online mechanism (email allowed until mechanism available)

rules.applies_to: All California employers (no size or industry exemption)
rules.verbatim_quote: Immediately means as soon as practically possible but not longer than 8 hours after the employer knows or with diligent inquiry would have known of the death or serious injury or illness. If the employer can demonstrate that exigent circumstances exist, the time frame for the report may be made no longer than 24 hours after the incident.
rules.notes: 14300.1/14300.2 confirm that even record-exempt employers must make this report. The CSLB Law Book (PDF p.46) restates: report 'immediately by telephone or email' (Labor Code 6409.1).

rules.title: Definition: serious injury or illness (reportable)
rules.plain_english: A serious injury or illness is one requiring inpatient hospitalization (other than for observation or diagnostic testing), or involving an amputation, loss of an eye, or serious permanent disfigurement. Public street/highway accidents are excluded unless in a construction zone.

parameters.excluded: accident on public street or highway, unless in a construction zone

rules.applies_to: All California employers
rules.verbatim_quote: “Serious injury or illness” means any injury or illness occurring in a place of employment or in connection with any employment that requires inpatient hospitalization for other than medical observation or diagnostic testing, or in which an employee suffers an amputation, the loss of an eye, or any serious degree of permanent disfigurement,
rules.notes: Highway accidents in a construction zone ARE reportable.

rules.title: Information to include in the Cal/OSHA serious injury report
rules.plain_english: When reporting, give (if available): time and date, employer name/address/phone, reporter's name and title, accident site address, on-site contact, injured employee name(s) and address, nature of injury, where the employee was taken, other agencies present, and a description including whether the scene was altered.
rules.applies_to: All California employers
rules.verbatim_quote: (10) Description of accident and whether the accident scene or instrumentality has been altered.

rules.title: Minimum $5,000 penalty for late/missed serious injury report
rules.plain_english: Failing to timely report an employee's serious injury, illness or death carries a minimum Cal/OSHA penalty of $5,000.

parameters.violation: failure to timely report under 8 CCR 342(a)

rules.applies_to: All California employers
rules.verbatim_quote: Any employer who fails to timely report an employee's injury or illness, or death, in violation of section 342(a) of Title 8 of the California Code of Regulations, shall be assessed a minimum penalty of $5,000.

rules.title: Employer's Report of Occupational Injury (Form 5020) within 5 days
rules.plain_english: For every work injury or illness causing lost time beyond the day of injury or needing treatment beyond first aid, file the employer's report with your workers' comp insurer (or DIR/DLSR if uninsured/self-insured) within five days after you learn of it. The report must include the employee's SSN.

parameters.trigger: employer obtains knowledge of injury/illness with lost time beyond date of injury or treatment beyond first aid
parameters.file_with: insurer if insured; otherwise DIR Division of Labor Statistics and Research

rules.applies_to: Employer-contractors with employees
rules.source_location: PDF page 45-46 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.verbatim_quote: An employer-contractor MUST file a complete report of every employee occupational injury or occupational illness that results in lost time beyond the date of injury or illness, or which requires medical treatment beyond first aid, with the Department of Industrial Relations through its Division of Labor Statistics and Research or, if an insured employer, with the insurer (Labor Code §6409.1).
rules.notes: Five-day deadline text continues on PDF p.46: '...within five days after the employer obtains knowledge of the injury or illness. Each report ... must indicate the Social Security number of the injured employee'. Form number 5020 is from the DIR WVPP guidance page; the Law Book says 'the form required by the Division of Labor Statistics and Research'. Failure to report to insurer can lead to WCAB order within five days; noncompliance punishable as contempt (Labor Code 3760).

rules.title: Post the Cal/OSHA 'Safety and Health Protection on the Job' notice
rules.plain_english: Post the Cal/OSHA notice in a conspicuous place. For construction, post it at each location where employees report each day. Not posting can bring a fine of up to $1,000 per violation.

parameters.notice_title: Safety and Health Protection on the Job
parameters.construction_posting_location: each location to which employees report each day

rules.applies_to: All employers; construction jobsites
rules.verbatim_quote: Where employers are engaged in activities which are physically dispersed such as construction or transportation, the notice required by this section shall be posted at each location to which employees report each day.
rules.notes: CSLB Law Book PDF p.46 also lists this posting duty (Labor Code 6408). Asbestos registration copy must be posted beside this poster (8 CCR 341.10(b)).

rules.title: Log 300 required if more than 10 employees at any time last year
rules.plain_english: If your company had more than 10 employees at any time during the last calendar year, you must keep Cal/OSHA injury and illness records (Forms 300, 300A, 301). Size is based on peak employment of the whole company.

parameters.measure: peak company-wide employment during last calendar year

rules.applies_to: All employers; construction is not an exempt industry
rules.verbatim_quote: (2) If your company had more than ten (10) employees at any time during the last calendar year, you must keep Cal/OSHA injury and illness records unless your establishment is classified as a partially exempt industry under Section 14300.2.
rules.notes: The 14300.2 Appendix A partially-exempt NAICS list (checked) contains no NAICS 23 (construction) codes.

rules.title: Record injuries on Form 300 and 301 within 7 calendar days
rules.plain_english: Enter each recordable injury or illness on the Cal/OSHA Form 300 Log and complete a Form 301 Incident Report within 7 calendar days of learning about it.

parameters.trigger: receiving information that a recordable case occurred

rules.applies_to: Employers required to keep Cal/OSHA injury and illness records (construction NAICS 23 is not industry-exempt; employers with 10 or fewer employees all last year are size-exempt)
rules.verbatim_quote: You must enter each recordable injury or illness on the Cal/OSHA Form 300 and Cal/OSHA Form 301 Incident Report within seven (7) calendar days of receiving information that a recordable injury or illness has occurred.
rules.notes: Privacy cases: enter 'privacy case' instead of the name and keep a separate confidential list.

rules.title: Jobsites lasting under a year can share one Form 300
rules.plain_english: Keep a separate Form 300 for each establishment expected to operate a year or longer. Short-term establishments (like most construction jobsites, under one year) may share one Form 300; each employee must be linked to an establishment. If records are kept centrally, transmit case info within 7 calendar days.
rules.applies_to: Employers required to keep Cal/OSHA injury and illness records (construction NAICS 23 is not industry-exempt; employers with 10 or fewer employees all last year are size-exempt)
rules.verbatim_quote: (a) Basic requirement. You must keep a separate Cal/OSHA Form 300 for each establishment that is expected to be in operation for one year or longer.

rules.title: Complete and certify Form 300A annual summary
rules.plain_english: At year end, review the Form 300, total it on Form 300A (zeros if no cases), include average employees and total hours worked, and have a company executive certify it (owner of a sole proprietorship/partnership, corporate officer, highest-ranking official at the establishment, or that person's supervisor).

certifier_roles: immediate supervisor of highest ranking official

rules.applies_to: Employers required to keep Cal/OSHA injury and illness records (construction NAICS 23 is not industry-exempt; employers with 10 or fewer employees all last year are size-exempt)
rules.verbatim_quote: A company executive must certify that he or she has examined the Cal/OSHA Form 300 and that he or she reasonably believes, based on his or her knowledge of the process by which the information was recorded, that the annual summary is correct and complete.

rules.title: Post Form 300A from February 1 to April 30
rules.plain_english: Post the certified annual summary (Form 300A) by February 1 of the following year and keep it posted until April 30, where employee notices are normally posted.

parameters.location: each establishment, conspicuous place where notices are customarily posted

rules.applies_to: Employers required to keep Cal/OSHA injury and illness records (construction NAICS 23 is not industry-exempt; employers with 10 or fewer employees all last year are size-exempt)
rules.verbatim_quote: You must post the annual summary no later than February 1 of the year following the year covered by the records and keep the posting in place until April 30.

rules.title: Present or mail Form 300A to employees who don't report weekly
rules.plain_english: Employees paid during February-April who don't report at least weekly to a location where the 300A is posted must be handed or mailed a copy of the summary.

parameters.trigger: employee receives pay during Feb-Apr posting period and does not report at least weekly to posting location

rules.applies_to: Employers required to keep Cal/OSHA injury and illness records (construction NAICS 23 is not industry-exempt; employers with 10 or fewer employees all last year are size-exempt); especially field/jobsite crews
rules.verbatim_quote: Employers are required to present or mail the annual summary to each employee who receives pay during the February through April posting period who does not normally report at least weekly to a location where the annual summary is posted

rules.title: Keep Forms 300, 300A, 301 for 5 years
rules.plain_english: Save the Form 300 log, privacy case list, 300A summary and 301 incident reports for five years after the end of the year they cover, and keep updating the stored Form 300 for newly discovered cases or changes.
rules.applies_to: Employers required to keep Cal/OSHA injury and illness records (construction NAICS 23 is not industry-exempt; employers with 10 or fewer employees all last year are size-exempt)
rules.verbatim_quote: (a) Basic requirement. You must save the Cal/OSHA Form 300, the privacy case list (if one exists), the Cal/OSHA Form 300A, and the Cal/OSHA Form 301 Incident Reports for five (5) years following the end of the calendar year that these records cover.

rules.title: Give employees copies of Form 300 by end of next business day
rules.plain_english: When an employee, former employee, personal representative or authorized employee representative asks for the Form 300 or 300A, provide copies by the end of the next business day. Injured employees get their own Form 301 by the end of the next business day; union representatives get 301s (redacted) within 7 calendar days.
rules.applies_to: Employers required to keep Cal/OSHA injury and illness records (construction NAICS 23 is not industry-exempt; employers with 10 or fewer employees all last year are size-exempt)
rules.verbatim_quote: you must give the requester a copy of the relevant Cal/OSHA 300 forms and annual summaries by the end of the next business day.

rules.title: Produce injury records to government within 4 business hours
rules.plain_english: When Cal/OSHA or another authorized government representative asks for your injury and illness records, provide access within four business hours, plus one free set of copies if requested.
rules.applies_to: Employers required to keep Cal/OSHA injury and illness records (construction NAICS 23 is not industry-exempt; employers with 10 or fewer employees all last year are size-exempt)
rules.verbatim_quote: When an authorized government representative asks for the records you keep under the provisions of this article, you must provide within four (4) business hours, access to the original recordkeeping documents requested as well as, if requested, one set of copies free of charge.

rules.title: Electronically submit injury data to OSHA by March 2
rules.plain_english: Construction establishments with 20-249 employees (and any establishment with 250+) must submit Form 300A data electronically to OSHA by March 2 each year. Establishments with 100+ employees in NAICS 2381 (foundation, structure and building exterior contractors) must also submit Form 300 and 301 data.

parameters.year: year after the calendar year covered
parameters.employee_count_basis: establishment peak at any time in previous calendar year; part-time/seasonal/temporary each count

rules.applies_to: Construction establishments meeting employee-count thresholds
rules.citation: 8 CCR 14300.41; Appendices H and I to 14300.48
rules.verbatim_quote: Establishments required to submit under paragraph (a)(1) or (2) of this section must submit all the required information by March 2 of the year after the calendar year covered by the form(s)
rules.notes: Appendix H (300A, 20-249 employees) lists NAICS 23 Construction; Appendix I (300/301 for 100+) lists only 2381 among construction codes. Both appendices read at https://www.dir.ca.gov/T8/14300_48_AppendixH.html and _AppendixI.html. Submission goes to OSHA's ITA website.

rules.title: Cal/OSHA permit: trenches/excavations 5 ft or deeper that people enter
rules.plain_english: Before constructing a trench or excavation 5 feet or deeper into which any person must descend, hold a Cal/OSHA annual or project permit. 'Descend' means entering any part once it reaches 5 feet.

parameters.trigger: any person required to descend into it

rules.applies_to: Employers constructing trenches/excavations (not government bodies or PUC-regulated utilities)
rules.verbatim_quote: (A) Construction of trenches or excavations 5 feet or deeper into which any person is required to descend. Note:For purposes of this subsection, “descend” means to enter any part of the trench or excavation once the excavation has attained a depth of 5 feet or more.
rules.notes: Exceptions (341(e)): government bodies; PUC-regulated public utilities; emergency repair of underground facilities; no one descends; graves; swimming pool excavation.

rules.title: Cal/OSHA permit: scaffolding, vertical shoring or falsework over 36 ft
rules.plain_english: Erecting scaffolding, vertical shoring, or falsework intended to be more than 36 feet high when completed requires a Cal/OSHA annual or project permit.
rules.applies_to: Employers erecting scaffolding, vertical shoring or falsework
rules.verbatim_quote: (B) Erection and placement of scaffolding, vertical shoring, or falsework intended to be more than 36 feet high when completed.

rules.title: Cal/OSHA permit: demolition of structures over 36 ft
rules.plain_english: To demolish or dismantle any building or structure more than 36 feet high, the project administrator (e.g., GC) must hold a project permit and every other employer doing demolition must hold an annual permit.

parameters.height_definition: top of structure incl. parapets/penthouses to lowest surrounding grade; excludes antennas, chimneys, flagpoles

rules.applies_to: Project administrators (GCs, prime contractors, owner-builders, CMs) and demolition subcontractors
rules.verbatim_quote: (3) To conduct the demolition or dismantling of any building or structure more than 36 feet in height, the Project Administrator shall hold a Project Permit and all other employers directly engaging in demolition or dismantling activity shall hold an Annual Permit.

rules.title: Cal/OSHA permit: erecting structures intended to exceed 36 ft
rules.plain_english: On a structure intended to be more than 36 feet high, the project administrator needs a project permit and each other employer doing structural steel/member erection, decking, curtain walls/precast/fascia, concrete forming/placement on steel, or structural/roof framing needs an annual permit.
rules.applies_to: Project administrators and trade employers on structures over 36 ft
rules.verbatim_quote: (4) To conduct any of the following activities on a structure intended to be more than 36 feet high when completed, the Project Administrator shall hold a Project Permit and all other employers directly engaging in these activities shall hold an Annual Permit:

rules.title: Cal/OSHA project permit: tower crane erection, climbing, dismantling
rules.plain_english: Erecting, raising/lowering (climbing) or dismantling a fixed tower crane requires a project permit held by the crane erector/climber/dismantler. A relocated crane on the same project needs a new permit. Notify Cal/OSHA at least 24 hours before erection, start of operation, climbing, and dismantling.
rules.applies_to: Tower crane erectors, climbers, dismantlers
rules.verbatim_quote: Note:The notification must be received by the Division at least 24 hours prior to the activity which is the subject of the notification and may be in writing or by telephone followed by written notification.
rules.notes: Application must certify a Division-licensed tower crane certifier/surveyor or manufacturer/distributor safety rep will be present during erection, climbing and dismantling.

rules.title: Annual permit vs project permit
rules.plain_english: There are two Cal/OSHA permit types. A project permit covers specific named site(s) and must be issued before permit-required work starts; one is needed per project while the holder stays project administrator. An annual permit lets an employer do specified permit-required work at any site for one year, but you must notify Cal/OSHA each time you start at a new site.

project_permit.where_to_apply: district office with jurisdiction over the site

annual_permit.expires: close of business day before issuance anniversary
annual_permit.where_to_apply: district office for employer's CA headquarters

rules.applies_to: Employers conducting permit-required activity
rules.verbatim_quote: (1) “Annual permit” means a permit issued pursuant to section 341.1(a)(2) that allows a qualifying employer to conduct specified permit-required activity at any jobsite for a period of one year.

rules.title: Annual permit holders: notify Cal/OSHA 24 hours before work at each new site
rules.plain_english: If you work under an annual permit, notify the Cal/OSHA district office with jurisdiction over the site at least 24 hours before starting the permit-required activity, giving the project location and the date and time work will start (mail, personal delivery, fax or email).

parameters.notify: Division district office with jurisdiction over the project site

rules.applies_to: Annual permit holders
rules.verbatim_quote: (B) The permit holder shall notify the Division district office that has jurisdiction over the site of the project at least 24 hours prior to the activity which is the subject of the notification.
rules.notes: The same 24-hour notice applies to each subsequent project under a multi-district project permit for essentially identical structures (341.1(f)(5)(D)).

rules.title: Cal/OSHA permit application contents
rules.plain_english: A permit application must include business contact info, a representative, the CSLB license number, proof of workers' comp, a check or money order for the fee (no cash/credit), a signed certification of knowledge of safety standards, and a description of safe work methods. Project permits also need the jobsite phone, address, start and completion dates, and activity description.
rules.applies_to: Permit applicants
rules.verbatim_quote: (C) A valid and applicable license number issued by the California Contractors State License Board, if applicable. (D) An attached copy of a current policy, binder or other proof of workers' compensation insurance, if applicable.
rules.notes: Cal/OSHA may require a safety conference; project permit issued within 5 working days of the conference if materials complete (341.1(e)(1)).

rules.title: Project permit issued within 5 working days of complete materials
rules.plain_english: Cal/OSHA must issue a project permit within five working days of the initial safety conference if your materials are complete, or within five working days of receiving complete materials (or deny in writing). Build this lead time into schedules.

parameters.clock_starts: initial safety conference with complete materials, or receipt of completed materials

rules.applies_to: Project permit applicants
rules.verbatim_quote: The Division shall issue the Project Permit within five working days of receiving complete application materials or deny the permit in writing pursuant to the requirements of Section 341.2.
rules.notes: Denial appeal: Director hearing within two working days of the appeal; rehearing requests within ten days of decision (341.2(b)-(c)).

rules.title: Cal/OSHA permit fees
rules.plain_english: Permit fees: $50 for excavation/trench, building/structure or scaffold/falsework, and demolition project permits; $350 for tower crane erection/climbing/dismantling; $100 for an annual permit.

parameters.payment: check or money order before issuance

rules.applies_to: Permit applicants
rules.verbatim_quote: (e) Annual permits as specified in section 341.1(e) of this article, for period January 1 to December 31 - $100.00.
rules.notes: 341.3(e) describes the annual permit fee period as Jan 1-Dec 31, while 341.1(h)(1) says an annual permit expires one year after issuance; flag the inconsistency to users.

rules.title: Post the Cal/OSHA permit at the jobsite
rules.plain_english: Post a copy of the permit at or near each place of employment. If posting at an excavation is impracticable, keep it available at the site at all times.

parameters.posting_location: at or near each place of employment
parameters.excavation_alternative: available at site at all times
parameters.mobile_unit_alternative: available at employer's head office in the district

rules.applies_to: Permit holders
rules.verbatim_quote: Any employer issued a permit pursuant to this Article shall post a copy or copies of the permit at or near each place of employment.

rules.title: Who/what is exempt from Cal/OSHA permits
rules.plain_english: Permit rules do not apply to government bodies, PUC-regulated public utilities, emergency repair trenches for underground facilities, excavations no one enters, graves, or swimming pool excavations.
rules.applies_to: Employers evaluating whether a permit is needed
rules.verbatim_quote: (6) Excavation for the construction of swimming pools.
rules.notes: Pool exemption applies to the permit only; excavation safety rules (1540-1547) still apply.

rules.title: Minimum $1,250 penalty for permit or asbestos registration violations
rules.plain_english: Violating Cal/OSHA permit requirements (trench, structure, demolition) or asbestos registration requirements carries a minimum proposed civil penalty of $1,250 (after adjustments, not below $250).
rules.applies_to: Employers subject to permit/registration rules
rules.verbatim_quote: shall be assessed a minimum proposed civil penalty of $1,250.

rules.title: Permit revocation/suspension: 24-hour hearing notice
rules.plain_english: Cal/OSHA can revoke or suspend a permit for good cause after a hearing; written notice must be served at least 24 hours before the hearing, and the employer must notify employees.
rules.applies_to: Permit holders
rules.verbatim_quote: (b) Notice shall be in writing and served upon the employer at least 24 hours in advance of the hearing.

rules.title: Cal/OSHA asbestos registration for 100+ sq ft jobs
rules.plain_english: Before starting asbestos-related work involving 100 square feet or more of asbestos-containing construction material (more than 0.1% asbestos by weight) at a single worksite, obtain a Cal/OSHA (DOSH) registration. It is valid for one year.

parameters.aggregation: sum noncontiguous locations at a single worksite (same hirer, single or multiple contracts)
parameters.not_aggregated: separate unrelated worksites each under 100 sq ft

rules.applies_to: Employers performing asbestos-related work (disturbing material >0.1% asbestos)
rules.verbatim_quote: (a) An employer who will be engaging in asbestos-related work, as defined, in subsection (b), involving 100 square feet or more of surface area of asbestos-containing material, computed in accordance with subsection (e) of this section, shall apply for and obtain a registration from the division prior to the commencement of any such work.
rules.notes: Routine maintenance where each component is under 100 sq ft is not aggregated. Work under 100 sq ft still requires 8 CCR 5203/5208 reporting.

rules.title: Asbestos registration application requirements
rules.plain_english: The registration application (under penalty of perjury) must include: CSLB asbestos certification if a contractor, proof of health insurance covering required medical exams (or a $500 trust account per asbestos worker) plus workers' comp, proof of required training/certification, and proof of knowledge and proper equipment.
rules.applies_to: Employers performing asbestos-related work (disturbing material >0.1% asbestos)
rules.verbatim_quote: Proof that sufficient health insurance coverage has been obtained to cover the entire cost of medical examinations and monitoring required by law or present proof that a $500 trust account has been provided for each employee engaged in such asbestos related work.

rules.title: Renew asbestos registration at least 30 days before expiration
rules.plain_english: File your asbestos registration renewal with Cal/OSHA no later than 30 days before the current registration expires.
rules.applies_to: Registered asbestos employers
rules.verbatim_quote: The application for renewal must be filed with the Division no later than thirty (30) days prior to the expiration date of the current registration.

rules.title: Asbestos registration fees: $350 new, $150 renewal
rules.plain_english: The Cal/OSHA asbestos registration application fee is $350; renewal is $150, paid before issuance.
rules.applies_to: Asbestos registration applicants
rules.verbatim_quote: (a) To cover the costs involved in investigating the registration application, and issuing the registration, an application fee of $350.00 is deemed reasonable and necessary.

rules.title: Cal/OSHA asbestos registration processing times
rules.plain_english: Cal/OSHA has 15 business days to tell you whether your registration application is complete, and 30 business days after a complete filing to decide.
rules.applies_to: Asbestos registration applicants
rules.verbatim_quote: (b) Within 30 business days from date of filing of a completed application, the Division shall inform the applicant in writing of its decision regarding the application.
rules.notes: Use for scheduling: apply at least ~45 business days before first registered job.

rules.title: Notify Cal/OSHA before each registered asbestos job
rules.plain_english: Give written notice to the nearest Cal/OSHA district office before starting each separate asbestos job or phase: address, exact location, projected start and completion dates, certified supervisor, qualified air-sampling person, and work description. Emergencies: phone first, then confirm in writing within 24 hours. Report changes at or before the change.
rules.applies_to: Registered asbestos employers
rules.verbatim_quote: written notice shall be provided to the nearest District Office of the Division prior to commencement of any such work activity, except where the circumstances require immediate abatement action in which case, the employer shall immediately notify the nearest district office by telephone or otherwise orally of the start of work, to be confirmed in writing no later than 24 hours thereafter.
rules.notes: 341.9 does not specify a fixed number of days' advance notice; it says 'prior to commencement'. (Separate EPA/air district NESHAP notifications are outside this file.)

rules.title: Asbestos jobsite sign and registration posting
rules.plain_english: Post a sign readable at 20 feet: 'Danger-Asbestos. Cancer and Lung Hazard. Keep Out.' Give a copy of the registration to the prime contractor and other employers before starting, and post it beside the Cal/OSHA poster.

parameters.sign_text: Danger-Asbestos. Cancer and Lung Hazard. Keep Out.

rules.applies_to: Registered asbestos employers
rules.verbatim_quote: (a) The employer shall post a sign readable at 20 feet at the location where any asbestos-related work subject to the registration and notification requirements of this article is to take place stating "Danger-Asbestos. Cancer and Lung Hazard. Keep Out."

rules.title: Pre-job asbestos safety conference
rules.plain_english: Hold a safety conference before starting asbestos work with representatives of the owner/contracting agency, contractor, employer, employees and employee representatives. Applies to all asbestos-handling jobs regardless of quantity.
rules.applies_to: Employers performing asbestos-related work (disturbing material >0.1% asbestos)
rules.verbatim_quote: The requirement of this section shall apply to all asbestos-handling jobs regardless of the amount of asbestos to be handled.

rules.title: CSLB: C-22 or asbestos certification required for 100+ sq ft
rules.plain_english: A contractor may not do asbestos-related work involving 100 sq ft or more of asbestos-containing material unless it holds the C-22 Asbestos Abatement classification or its qualifier passed the CSLB asbestos certification exam. A non-certified contractor may bid and contract if the asbestos work is performed by a C-22 or certified and registered contractor.
rules.applies_to: CSLB licensees
rules.source_location: PDF page 274-275 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.verbatim_quote: A contractor shall not engage in asbestos-related work, as defined in Section 6501.8 of the Labor Code, that involves 100 square feet or more of surface area of asbestos containing materials, unless the contractor holds a C-22 Asbestos Abatement classification or the qualifier for the license passes an asbestos certification examination.
rules.notes: B&P 7058.6: register with DOSH within 90 days of being notified of passing the certification exam; proof of current DOSH registration required at license renewal if doing asbestos work.

rules.title: C-22 licensees: submit DOSH registration proof within 90 days
rules.plain_english: A new C-22 Asbestos Abatement licensee must give CSLB proof of DOSH registration within 90 days of license issuance; no abatement work until proof is submitted. Missing the deadline automatically suspends the license or removes the C-22. Renewal also requires proof of current DOSH registration.

parameters.consequence: automatic suspension or removal of C-22

rules.applies_to: C-22 Asbestos Abatement contractors
rules.source_location: PDF page 465-466 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.verbatim_quote: Failure of a licensee to provide proof of current registration with DOSH within 90 days after issuance shall result in the automatic suspension of the license or removal of the C-22—asbestos abatement contractor classification at the end of the 90 days.
rules.notes: C-22 holders must complete DOSH registration training per 8 CCR 1529. C-22 excludes hazardous substance removal (B&P 7058.7).

rules.title: Penalty: asbestos work without CSLB certification
rules.plain_english: Doing asbestos-related work without the required certification is a misdemeanor: first offense $1,000-$3,000 fine and possible license action; subsequent offense $3,000-$5,000 and/or up to one year in county jail plus mandatory license suspension or revocation.
rules.applies_to: Licensed or unlicensed contractors
rules.source_location: PDF page 246 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.verbatim_quote: (a) Conviction of a first offense is punishable by a fine of not less than one thousand dollars ($1,000) or more than three thousand dollars ($3,000), and by possible revocation or suspension of any contractor’s license.

rules.title: Penalty: contracting with an uncertified asbestos contractor
rules.plain_english: A contractor who knowingly, negligently, or by failing to inquire contracts with someone who lacks required asbestos certification faces a $1,000-$3,000 infraction (first offense); a subsequent offense is a misdemeanor with $3,000-$5,000 fine and/or up to 1 year jail and required license action.

parameters.standard: knowingly, negligently, or by failure to inquire

rules.applies_to: Contractors hiring subcontractors for asbestos work
rules.source_location: PDF page 357 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.verbatim_quote: (a) Conviction of a first offense is an infraction punishable by a fine of not less than one thousand dollars ($1,000) or more than three thousand dollars ($3,000), and by possible revocation or suspension of any contractor’s license.
rules.notes: Software check: verify sub's CSLB asbestos certification/C-22 and DOSH registration before awarding asbestos scope.

rules.title: Asbestos removal ads must show certification and registration numbers
rules.plain_english: Anyone advertising asbestos removal services must be CSLB-certified and DOSH-registered, and every ad must show both numbers using the same name under which certified/registered.
rules.applies_to: Contractors advertising asbestos removal
rules.source_location: PDF page 346 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.verbatim_quote: Each advertisement shall include that person’s certification and registration numbers and shall use the same name under which that person is certified and registered.

rules.title: Asbestos inspection reports: disclose financial ties to abatement firms
rules.plain_english: A contractor doing an asbestos inspection required for a loan or permit must disclose orally and in writing any ownership or financial relationship (including referral fees) with a company that does the corrective work. Violation: $3,000-$5,000 fine and/or up to 1 year jail.

triggers: report required for loan secured by property
report required by public entity for permit

rules.applies_to: Contractors performing asbestos inspections
rules.source_location: PDF page 356-357 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.verbatim_quote: the contractor shall disclose orally and in writing if it is owned or has any common ownership, or any financial relationship whatsoever, including, but not limited to, commissions or referral fees, with an entity in the business of performing the corrective work.

rules.title: Asbestos exposure limits: 0.1 f/cc TWA, 1.0 f/cc 30-minute excursion
rules.plain_english: No employee may be exposed above 0.1 fiber per cubic centimeter as an 8-hour TWA, or above 1.0 f/cc averaged over 30 minutes.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose work involves asbestos
rules.verbatim_quote: The employer shall ensure that no employee is exposed to an airborne concentration of asbestos in excess of 0.1 fiber per cubic centimeter of air as an eight (8) hour time-weighted average (TWA)

rules.title: Asbestos competent person; Class I inspections every shift
rules.plain_english: Designate a competent person on every asbestos construction worksite. For Class I work (removing TSI and surfacing ACM/PACM), the competent person must inspect at least once each work shift and whenever employees ask.

class_definitions.I: removal of TSI and surfacing ACM/PACM
class_definitions.II: removal of other ACM (e.g., floor tile, roofing, wallboard, mastics)

rules.applies_to: Employers performing asbestos-related work (disturbing material >0.1% asbestos)
rules.verbatim_quote: For Class I jobs, on-site inspections shall be made at least once during each work shift, and at any time at employee request.

rules.title: Tell employees asbestos monitoring results within 5 working days
rules.plain_english: Notify affected employees of asbestos air monitoring results, in writing individually or by posting, no later than 5 working days after you receive them, including corrective action if a limit was exceeded.
rules.applies_to: Employers performing asbestos-related work (disturbing material >0.1% asbestos)
rules.verbatim_quote: (A) As soon as possible but not later than 5 working days following receipt of monitoring results required by this section, the employer shall notify affected employees of the monitoring results.

rules.title: Asbestos medical surveillance at 30+ days per year
rules.plain_english: Provide medical surveillance for employees who do Class I, II or III work, or are exposed at/above the PEL, for a combined total of 30 or more days per year; exam due within 10 working days after the 30th day.

parameters.excluded_days: Class II/III on intact material for 1 hour or less with full work practices

rules.applies_to: Employers performing asbestos-related work (disturbing material >0.1% asbestos)
rules.verbatim_quote: The employer shall institute a medical surveillance program for all employees who, for a combined total of 30 or more days per year, are engaged in Class I, II and III work or are exposed at or above the permissible exposure limit.

rules.title: Asbestos records: 30 years exposure, employment+30 medical, training +1 year
rules.plain_english: Keep asbestos exposure monitoring records at least 30 years, medical records for duration of employment plus 30 years, and training records 1 year beyond last employment. If you go out of business with no successor, notify the Director 90 days before disposal.

parameters.training_records: 1 year beyond last date of employment

rules.applies_to: Employers performing asbestos-related work (disturbing material >0.1% asbestos)
rules.verbatim_quote: (4) Training records. The employer shall maintain all employee training records for one (1) year beyond the last date of employment by that employer.

rules.title: Lead in construction: PEL 10 ug/m3, action level 2 ug/m3 (since Jan 1, 2025)
rules.plain_english: California's amended lead standard lowered the permissible exposure limit to 10 micrograms per cubic meter (8-hour TWA) and the action level to 2 ug/m3. Abrasive blasting has a temporary 25 ug/m3 limit until January 1, 2030.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose work may expose employees to lead
rules.verbatim_quote: (1) The employer shall ensure that no employee is exposed to an airborne concentration of lead greater than 10 micrograms per cubic meter of air (10 µg/m³) calculated as an 8-hour time-weighted average (TWA).
rules.notes: Amendment filed 4-8-2024, operative 1-1-2025. Some (d)(6) monitoring tiers still reference 30 and 50 ug/m3. Older guidance citing PEL 50 / AL 30 is superseded.

rules.title: Lead work: written notice to Cal/OSHA 24 hours before trigger tasks
rules.plain_english: When planned work includes lead trigger tasks, the nearest Cal/OSHA district office must receive written notice at least 24 hours before work starts (letter, fax, email, or phone followed by written notice within 24 hours). Not required if under 100 sq ft/100 linear ft disturbed, only torch cutting/welding up to 1 hour per shift, or material under 0.5% lead (5,000 ppm or 1.0 mg/cm2).
rules.applies_to: Construction employers performing lead trigger tasks (8 CCR 1532.1(d)(2))
rules.verbatim_quote: (1) The employer shall ensure that the information required by subsection (p)(2) is received by the nearest Cal/OSHA District Office at least 24 hours prior to the commencement of the work by any of the following means:
rules.notes: Urgent unforeseen lead work within 24 hours: phone notice before start plus written notice within 24 hours. Changes to start date, area, or work type must be reported before or upon the change.

rules.title: Lead: written compliance program before the job, updated every 6 months
rules.plain_english: Before starting the job, establish a written lead compliance program (activities, controls, monitoring data, schedule, work practices, multi-contractor arrangements) and revise it at least every 6 months. Keep it available at the worksite.

parameters.timing: prior to commencement of the job

rules.applies_to: Construction employers with lead exposures covered by 1532.1(e)
rules.verbatim_quote: (E) Written programs shall be revised and updated at least every 6 months to reflect the current status of the program.
rules.notes: The trigger language preceding (e)(2)(A) (exposure above the PEL) was not separately quoted; confirm applicability for jobs below PEL.

rules.title: Lead air monitoring frequency by exposure level
rules.plain_english: Repeat lead monitoring: below action level - none (unless changes); at/above action level but below 30 ug/m3 - every 12 months; 30-50 ug/m3 - every 6 months; above 50 ug/m3 - quarterly. Stop only after two consecutive results at least 7 days apart fall below the tier.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers with lead exposures
rules.verbatim_quote: (B) If the initial determination or subsequent determination reveals employee exposure to be at or above the action level but below 30 µg/m³ as an 8-hour TWA, the employer shall perform monitoring at least every 12 months.

rules.title: Lead medical surveillance and blood lead testing
rules.plain_english: Provide medical surveillance for employees exposed at/above the action level (exceptions for fewer than 30 days in 12 months with no day over 10 ug/m3, or fewer than 15 days with no day over 20 ug/m3) and as interim protection for trigger tasks. Blood lead testing every 2 months for the first 6 months, then every 6 months; more often for elevated levels.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers with lead exposures
rules.verbatim_quote: Exception 1: Medical surveillance is not required for an employee who is not exposed to lead at or above the action level for 30 or more days in any 12 consecutive months, and who is not exposed on any day above 10 µg/m³ as an 8-hour TWA, without regard to respirator use.

rules.title: Lead medical removal at blood lead 30 ug/dl
rules.plain_english: Remove an employee from lead exposure when their last blood lead test is 30 ug/dl or higher, or (from Jan 1, 2026) the last two blood lead tests are 20 ug/dl or higher, or the 6-month average is 20 ug/dl or higher (unless the last test is below 15). Return after two tests at least 30 days apart below 15 ug/dl.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers with lead exposures
rules.verbatim_quote: 1. The last blood lead test indicates that the employee's blood lead level is at or above 30 µg/dl;

rules.title: Silica in construction: covered unless always below 25 ug/m3
rules.plain_english: The construction silica standard covers all respirable crystalline silica exposures in construction unless exposure will stay below 25 ug/m3 (8-hour TWA) under any foreseeable conditions.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers (cutting, drilling, grinding concrete, masonry, stone, etc.)
rules.verbatim_quote: (a) Scope and application. This section applies to all occupational exposures to respirable crystalline silica in construction work, except where employee exposure will remain below 25 micrograms per cubic meter of air (25 μg/m³) as an 8-hour time-weighted average (TWA) under any foreseeable conditions.

rules.title: Silica: follow Table 1 controls or meet PEL of 50 ug/m3
rules.plain_english: For tasks on Table 1, fully implement the listed engineering controls, work practices and respirators. Otherwise, assess exposures and keep them at or below the 50 ug/m3 PEL (8-hour TWA).

compliance_paths: exposure assessment + PEL (performance or scheduled monitoring)

rules.applies_to: Construction employers with silica exposure
rules.verbatim_quote: (1) Permissible exposure limit (PEL). The employer shall ensure that no employee is exposed to an airborne concentration of respirable crystalline silica in excess of 50 μg/m³, calculated as an 8-hour TWA.

rules.title: Silica: written exposure control plan, reviewed annually
rules.plain_english: Have a written silica exposure control plan describing silica tasks, controls and respirators for each task, housekeeping, and procedures to restrict access. Review it at least annually and designate a competent person to inspect jobsites regularly.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers covered by 1532.3
rules.verbatim_quote: (2) The employer shall review and evaluate the effectiveness of the written exposure control plan at least annually and update it as necessary.

rules.title: Silica: designate a competent person
rules.plain_english: Designate a competent person to make frequent and regular inspections of jobsites, materials and equipment to implement the silica exposure control plan.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers covered by 1532.3
rules.verbatim_quote: (4) The employer shall designate a competent person to make frequent and regular inspections of job sites, materials, and equipment to implement the written exposure control plan.

rules.title: Silica medical surveillance for respirator use 30+ days/year
rules.plain_english: Offer free medical exams to employees required to wear a respirator for silica 30 or more days per year: baseline within 30 days of assignment (unless one in last 3 years), then at least every 3 years.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers covered by 1532.3
rules.verbatim_quote: (A) The employer shall make medical surveillance available at no cost to the employee, and at a reasonable time and place, for each employee who will be required under this section to use a respirator for 30 or more days per year.

rules.title: Silica: no dry sweeping or compressed-air cleaning
rules.plain_english: Don't allow dry sweeping/brushing where it could add to silica exposure unless wet sweeping or HEPA vacuuming isn't feasible, and don't use compressed air to clean clothing or surfaces unless used with effective dust capture ventilation.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers covered by 1532.3
rules.verbatim_quote: (1) The employer shall not allow dry sweeping or dry brushing where such activity could contribute to employee exposure to respirable crystalline silica unless wet sweeping, HEPA-filtered vacuuming or other methods that minimize the likelihood of exposure are not feasible.

rules.title: Fall protection required above 7.5 feet
rules.plain_english: Employees exposed to falls of more than 7 1/2 feet from a structure's perimeter, unprotected sides/edges, leading edges, shaftways/openings, roofs steeper than 7:12, or other surfaces steeper than 40 degrees must wear approved personal fall arrest, restraint or positioning systems unless otherwise adequately protected.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers
rules.verbatim_quote: (a) Approved personal fall arrest, personal fall restraint or positioning systems shall be worn by those employees whose work exposes them to falling in excess of 7 1/2 feet from the perimeter of a structure, unprotected sides and edges, leading edges, through shaftways and openings, sloped roof surfaces steeper than 7:12,
rules.notes: Trade-specific triggers differ: residential framing/roofing 6 ft (1716.2, 1731); commercial roofing 20 ft (1730).

rules.title: Site-specific written Fall Protection Plan when conventional protection is infeasible
rules.plain_english: If you can show guardrails, fall arrest and nets are infeasible or create a greater hazard, you may use a written, site-specific fall protection plan prepared by a qualified person, kept current and on site, implemented under a competent person, listing reasons, alternative measures, controlled access zones, and the employees allowed in them. Investigate and update after any fall or near miss.

parameters.presumption: conventional fall protection is feasible; employer bears burden

rules.applies_to: Construction employers using a fall protection plan
rules.verbatim_quote: (1) The fall protection plan shall be prepared by a qualified person and developed specifically for the site where the construction work is being performed and the plan must be maintained up to date. The plan shall document the identity of the qualified person.
rules.notes: Amended 11-26-2024, operative 7-1-2025: scope now 'all construction operations' where conventional fall protection is shown infeasible or a greater hazard.

rules.title: Residential/light commercial framing: fall protection at 6 feet
rules.plain_english: When walking/working on top plates, joists, rafters, trusses or beams 6 feet or more above grade or the floor below, provide scaffolding, guardrails, nets, personal fall protection, or (if conventional methods are infeasible) a fall protection plan with safety monitors and controlled access zones.
rules.applies_to: Residential-type and light commercial framing (joists/trusses on stud walls)
rules.verbatim_quote: (1) When employees are walking/working on top plates, joists, rafters, trusses, beams or other similar structural members 6 feet or more above the surrounding grade or floor level below, fall protection shall be provided by one or more of the following methods:

rules.title: Residential roofing: fall protection at 6 feet (any height above 7:12)
rules.plain_english: On residential-type roofing with slopes up to 7:12, protect employees when the fall distance is 6 feet or more; on slopes steeper than 7:12, protection is required regardless of height.
rules.applies_to: Residential-type roofing (single-family, townhouses, duplexes)
rules.verbatim_quote: (1) Roof slopes 0:12 up to and including 7:12. Employees shall be protected from falling when on a roof surface where the employee fall distance is 6 feet or more above the grade or level below

rules.title: Non-residential roofing: fall protection on roofs over 20 feet
rules.plain_english: For non-residential roofing operations, protect employees from falls from roofs more than 20 feet high (warning lines at least 5 ft from edge on low-slope roofs; any height when using felt-laying machines pulled by an operator walking backwards).
rules.applies_to: Roofing operations other than residential-type (8 CCR 1731)
rules.verbatim_quote: (1) Employees shall be protected from falls from roofs of a height of more than 20 feet by use of one or a combination of the methods in this section.

rules.title: Cave-in protection for excavations 5 feet or deeper
rules.plain_english: Every employee in an excavation must be protected by an adequate protective system (sloping, benching, shoring, shielding) unless it is entirely in stable rock, or less than 5 feet deep and a competent person finds no sign of potential cave-in.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers with employees in excavations
rules.verbatim_quote: (B) Excavations are less than 5 feet in depth and examination of the ground by a competent person provides no indication of a potential cave-in.

rules.title: Trench egress within 25 feet when 4 feet or deeper
rules.plain_english: Trenches 4 feet or deeper must have a stairway, ladder, ramp or other safe way out so no employee has to travel more than 25 feet laterally to reach it. Test atmospheres before entry over 4 feet where hazardous atmospheres could exist.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers with employees in trenches
rules.verbatim_quote: A stairway, ladder, ramp or other safe means of egress shall be located in trench excavations that are 4 feet or more in depth so as to require no more than 25 feet of lateral travel for employees.

rules.title: Daily competent-person excavation inspections
