rules.plain_english: A competent person must inspect excavations, adjacent areas and protective systems daily before work starts, as needed during the shift, and after every rainstorm or other hazard-increasing event; remove employees if cave-in or hazardous conditions are found.

parameters.frequency: daily, prior to start of work, as needed through shift

rules.applies_to: Construction employers with employees in excavations
rules.verbatim_quote: An inspection shall be conducted by the competent person prior to the start of work and as needed throughout the shift. Inspections shall also be made after every rain storm or other hazard increasing occurrence.

rules.title: Notify regional notification center (811) at least 2 working days before digging
rules.plain_english: Cal/OSHA's excavation order requires advising all regional notification centers (USA North/DigAlert via 811) and known non-member facility owners at least 2 working days before any digging, except emergency repairs.
rules.applies_to: Excavators
rules.verbatim_quote: (2) All Regional Notification Centers as defined by Government Code Section 4216(j) in the area involved and all known owners of subsurface facilities in the area who are not members of a Notification Center shall be advised of the proposed work at least 2 working days prior to the start of any digging or excavation work.
rules.notes: The 14-calendar-day maximum and 28-day ticket validity are from the CSLB Law Book (PDF pages 84-85) summary of Gov. Code 4216; Gov. Code fines up to $10,000 negligent / $50,000 knowing and willful (PDF p.86).

rules.title: Keep spoil and equipment at least 2 feet from excavation edge
rules.plain_english: Keep excavated material and equipment at least 2 feet back from the edge, or use retaining devices, to keep it from falling into the excavation.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers with excavations
rules.verbatim_quote: Protection shall be provided by placing and keeping such materials or equipment at least 2 feet from the edge of excavations, or by the use of retaining devices that are sufficient to prevent materials or equipment from falling or rolling into excavations, or by a combination of both if necessary.

rules.title: Falsework/shoring: CA civil engineer design over 14 ft height or 16 ft span
rules.plain_english: Falsework or vertical shoring needs design calculations and working drawings signed by a California-registered civil engineer if it is more than 14 feet high (sills to soffit), has spans over 16 feet, or carries vehicle/rail traffic through it. Others may be approved by a CE, manufacturer's rep, or qualified contractor rep. Keep the plan on site; inspect and certify in writing before concrete placement.
rules.applies_to: Employers erecting falsework or vertical shoring
rules.verbatim_quote: (A) The height, as measured from the top of the sills to the soffit of the superstructure exceeds 14 feet. (B) Individual horizontal span lengths exceed 16 feet.
rules.notes: Falsework over 36 ft also needs a Cal/OSHA permit (8 CCR 341(d)(5)(B)).

rules.title: Scaffold erection/dismantling supervised by a qualified person; daily plank inspection
rules.plain_english: Scaffold erection and dismantling must be supervised and directed by a qualified person, and scaffold planks must be visually inspected for defects before use each day.

parameters.engineered_scaffold_designer: CA-registered civil engineer experienced in scaffold design

rules.applies_to: Employers erecting or using scaffolds
rules.verbatim_quote: (1) The erection and dismantling of scaffolds or falsework shall be performed under the supervision and direction of a qualified person.

rules.title: Cranes over 3 tons: annual certification by licensed certifier
rules.plain_english: Cranes and derricks in lifting service over 3 tons rated capacity may not be used until you confirm they have current annual (and quadrennial) certificates from a Cal/OSHA-licensed certifying agency.
rules.applies_to: Employers using cranes/derricks
rules.verbatim_quote: (1) Tests and examinations shall be conducted annually by a currently licensed certificating agency or designee listed in the certificating agency license, and a certificate shall be issued by the certificating agency;

rules.title: Construction crane operators: certification, renewed every 5 years
rules.plain_english: Crane operators in construction must be trained, certified (accredited certifying entity, valid up to 5 years) or government-licensed, and evaluated before operating; employers pay for certification. Re-certify every 5 years (1,000 documented hours waives the hands-on exam). Trainees work only under continuous monitoring with restrictions.
rules.applies_to: Employers operating cranes/derricks in construction
rules.verbatim_quote: (1) Certification. Certificates shall be valid for a maximum of five (5) years.
rules.notes: Former Construction Safety Orders Article 15 crane sections (1610-1619) were repealed effective 7-26-2022; construction crane rules now sit in GISO Group 13 (e.g., 5006.2).

rules.title: Appropriately trained first-aid persons available
rules.plain_english: Each employer must ensure enough appropriately trained persons are available to give first aid; employers on a multi-employer site may pool trained persons if the pool covers the combined workforce.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers
rules.verbatim_quote: (b) Appropriately Trained Person. Each employer shall ensure the availability of a suitable number of appropriately trained persons to render first aid.
rules.notes: Rule states no fixed ratio or response-time threshold.

rules.title: First-aid kit in weatherproof container, contents by crew size
rules.plain_english: Every employer with personnel on a construction project must provide at least one first-aid kit in a weatherproof container, inspected regularly and restocked. Minimum contents are set by a licensed physician or by the table in 1512 based on crew size (1-5, 6-15, 16-200, over 200). No drugs or medicines without written physician approval.

items_16_plus: sterile surgical pads for pressure dressings

rules.applies_to: Construction employers
rules.verbatim_quote: (1) Every employer working on or furnishing personnel on a construction project, on line crews and on other short duration or transient jobs shall provide at least one first-aid kit in a weatherproof container.

rules.title: Post emergency phone numbers at the job phone
rules.plain_english: Post the phone numbers of a physician (plus an alternate if available), hospitals, ambulance and fire services near the job telephone, or otherwise make them available. Inform all employees of what to do in case of injury or illness and provide transport or communication to get emergency care.

parameters.location: near job telephone or switchboard, or otherwise available

rules.applies_to: Construction employers
rules.verbatim_quote: The telephone numbers of the following emergency services in the area shall be posted near the job telephone, telephone switchboard, or otherwise made available to the employees where no job site telephone exists:

rules.title: Written emergency medical services plan
rules.plain_english: Have a written plan describing how you meet the emergency medical service requirements; employers sharing a combined program may use one plan.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers
rules.verbatim_quote: (i) Written Plan. The employer shall have a written plan to provide emergency medical services. The plan shall specify the means of implementing all applicable requirements in this section.

rules.title: Two-way emergency call system and basket litter at 5 floors / 48 ft
rules.plain_english: Buildings or structures five or more floors or 48 feet or more above or below ground need a two-way voice emergency communication system and at least one basket litter with straps and two blankets.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers on multi-story or deep projects
rules.verbatim_quote: (g) Emergency Call Systems. A two-way voice emergency communication system shall be installed, for buildings and structures five or more floors or 48 feet or more above or below ground level, to notify persons designated in the emergency medical services plan.

rules.title: Jobsite toilets: 1 per 20 employees of each sex
rules.plain_english: Provide at least one separate toilet facility per 20 employees (or fraction) of each sex; with fewer than 5 employees one all-gender single-user toilet is enough. Mobile crews with ready transport to nearby toilets are exempt.

parameters.rounding: per 20 or fraction thereof, each sex

rules.applies_to: Construction jobsites
rules.verbatim_quote: (a) A minimum of one separate toilet facility shall be provided for each 20 employees or fraction thereof of each sex.

rules.title: Jobsite washing stations: 1 per 20 employees
rules.plain_english: Provide at least one washing station (water, soap, single-use towels or blower) per 20 employees or fraction, located so anyone using a toilet can readily wash.
rules.applies_to: Construction jobsites
rules.verbatim_quote: A minimum of one washing station shall be provided for each twenty employees or fraction thereof.

rules.title: Written Hazard Communication program (incl. multi-employer sites)
rules.plain_english: Keep a written hazard communication program at the workplace covering labels, safety data sheets and training. On multi-employer sites it must explain how you will inform other employers of hazardous chemicals their workers may be exposed to.
rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees may be exposed to hazardous chemicals
rules.verbatim_quote: (1) Employers shall develop, implement, and maintain at the workplace a written hazard communication program for their employees which at least describes how the criteria specified in sections 5194(f), (g), and (h) for labels and other forms of warning, safety data sheets, and employee information and training will be met,

rules.title: Written respiratory protection program; annual fit testing
rules.plain_english: Where respirators are necessary or required (e.g., silica, lead, asbestos), have a written worksite-specific respiratory protection program with a trained administrator, and fit-test tight-fitting respirators before first use, when changing models, and at least annually.
rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees use required respirators
rules.verbatim_quote: (2) The employer shall ensure that an employee using a tight-fitting facepiece respirator is fit tested prior to initial use of the respirator, whenever a different respirator facepiece (size, style, model or make) is used, and at least annually thereafter.

rules.title: Written Workplace Violence Prevention Plan (SB 553) since July 1, 2024
rules.plain_english: Covered employers must establish, implement and maintain an effective written Workplace Violence Prevention Plan (WVPP), either stand-alone or as a separate section of the IIPP, specific to each work area and operation. Required elements include responsible persons, employee involvement, coordination with other employers, compliance, communication, reporting without retaliation, emergency response, training, hazard identification and correction, post-incident investigation, and periodic review.
rules.applies_to: All California employers, places of employment and employer-provided housing, except Labor Code 6401.9(b)(2) exemptions (construction employers are covered)
rules.verbatim_quote: On September 30, 2023, California Senate Bill 553 (Cortese) was signed into law and California Labor Code section 6401.9 will be in effect and enforceable on July 1, 2024. Employers that fall within the scope of this law must establish, implement, and maintain an effective written Workplace Violence Prevention Plan
rules.notes: Read from official Cal/OSHA (dir.ca.gov) guidance pages summarizing LC 6401.9; leginfo.legislature.ca.gov statute text was not reachable from this environment. As of the 2026-10-27 DIR rulemaking page, the implementing regulation (proposed 8 CCR 3343) was still a discussion draft (OSHSB deadline to adopt: 2026-12-31). Re-check for an adopted 3343 in 2027.

rules.title: Violent incident log for every workplace violence incident
rules.plain_english: Record every workplace violence incident (including threats) in a violent incident log, with no personal identifying information. On multi-employer sites, the model plan also has you give a copy of the log to the controlling employer.
rules.applies_to: All California employers, places of employment and employer-provided housing, except Labor Code 6401.9(b)(2) exemptions (construction employers are covered)
rules.verbatim_quote: All workplace violence incidents are required to be documented in the violent incident log.
rules.notes: Cal/OSHA FAQ (official dir.ca.gov). Employers may design their own log if it captures the LC 6401.9(d)(2) fields. Multi-employer provision is from Cal/OSHA's Model WVPP (https://www.dir.ca.gov/dosh/dosh_publications/Model-WPV-Plan-General-Industry.docx).

rules.title: Workplace violence training: initial and annually
rules.plain_english: Provide WVPP training when the plan is first established, annually thereafter, and when new hazards are identified or the plan changes. Training had to be in place by July 1, 2024.
rules.applies_to: All California employers, places of employment and employer-provided housing, except Labor Code 6401.9(b)(2) exemptions (construction employers are covered)
rules.verbatim_quote: Annually to ensure all employees understand and comply with the plan.
rules.notes: Quote is from Cal/OSHA's official Model WVPP (dir.ca.gov). The statutory 'initial training ... and annually thereafter' wording also appears as baseline LC 6401.9 text in DIR's draft comparison document (https://www.dir.ca.gov/dosh/doshreg/Workplace-Violence-in-General-Industry/WPV-Draft-Revisions-May-13-2025.docx). FAQ Q21 confirms training was enforceable July 1, 2024 with no grace period.

rules.title: Workplace violence records: 5 years (training 1 year)
rules.plain_english: Keep workplace violence hazard identification/evaluation/correction records, violent incident logs, and incident investigation records for at least 5 years; keep WVPP training records for at least 1 year. Records must not contain medical information.
rules.applies_to: All California employers, places of employment and employer-provided housing, except Labor Code 6401.9(b)(2) exemptions (construction employers are covered)
rules.verbatim_quote: Records of workplace violence hazard identification, evaluation, and correction, for a minimum of five years.
rules.notes: Same DIR page lists, as separate bullets: training records minimum one year; Violence Incident Logs minimum five years; incident investigation records minimum five years. Official Cal/OSHA guidance page summarizing LC 6401.9(f); training records must include dates, contents/summary, trainer names and qualifications, and attendee names and job titles (per DIR draft baseline text and Model WVPP).

rules.title: Give employees WVPP records within 15 calendar days
rules.plain_english: Workplace violence hazard records, training records and violent incident logs must be made available to employees and their representatives on request, free, for examination and copying within 15 calendar days.

parameters.division_access: all WVP records incl. investigations upon request

rules.applies_to: All California employers, places of employment and employer-provided housing, except Labor Code 6401.9(b)(2) exemptions (construction employers are covered)
rules.verbatim_quote: All records of workplace violence hazard identification, evaluation, and correction, as well as training records and violent incident logs, shall be made available to employees and their authorized representatives, upon request and without cost, for examination and copying within 15 calendar days of a request.

rules.title: Review the WVPP at least annually and after incidents
rules.plain_english: Review the Workplace Violence Prevention Plan for effectiveness at least annually, when a deficiency becomes apparent, and after a workplace violence incident.
rules.applies_to: All California employers, places of employment and employer-provided housing, except Labor Code 6401.9(b)(2) exemptions (construction employers are covered)
rules.verbatim_quote: At least annually. When a deficiency is observed or becomes apparent. After a workplace violence incident.
rules.notes: Read in Cal/OSHA's official Model WVPP; DIR's draft-vs-statute comparison shows the same 'annually, when a deficiency is observed or becomes apparent, and after a workplace incident' review language.

rules.title: Workplace violence injury: workers' comp notice within one working day
rules.plain_english: After a workplace violence incident, give the injured employee notice of workers' compensation eligibility within one working day; also log it, investigate, report serious injuries within 8 hours, and record it on the Form 300 if recordable.
rules.applies_to: All California employers, places of employment and employer-provided housing, except Labor Code 6401.9(b)(2) exemptions (construction employers are covered)
rules.verbatim_quote: Employers must give employees notice of workers' compensation eligibility within one working day of a workplace violence incident.
rules.notes: The CSLB Law Book (PDF p.47) separately notes the Labor Code 3553 duty to notify workplace-crime victims of workers' comp eligibility.

rules.title: WVPP exemptions (Labor Code 6401.9(b)(2))
rules.plain_english: Exempt from the WVPP law: health care settings covered by 8 CCR 3342, certain CDCR facilities and POST-certified law enforcement agencies complying with 3203, employees teleworking from a location of their choice not controlled by the employer, and places of employment with fewer than 10 employees working there at any given time that are not accessible to the public and comply with 3203.
rules.applies_to: All California employers, places of employment and employer-provided housing, except Labor Code 6401.9(b)(2) exemptions (construction employers are covered)
rules.verbatim_quote: Places of employment where there are less than 10 employees working at the place at any given time and that are not accessible to the public, if the places are in compliance with Section 3203 of Title 8 of the California Code of Regulations.
rules.notes: The quoted sentence is the LC 6401.9 baseline text shown (as a proposed deletion) in DIR's official May 13, 2025 draft-revisions comparison document; the statute itself on leginfo was not reachable, so marked not read from primary statutory text. Most active construction jobsites are 'accessible to the public' in some sense or exceed 10 workers; treat the small-site exemption as narrow and employer-proven. Proposed 8 CCR 3343 would change the headcount test (draft only).

rules.title: Cal/OSHA civil penalty amounts (2025 schedule)
rules.plain_english: Cal/OSHA penalties: regulatory and general violations up to $16,285 each; serious violations up to $25,000 (base $18,000); repeat violations multiplied x2/x4/x10 up to $162,851; willful violations multiplied x5 with a minimum of $11,632 and maximum of $162,851.
rules.applies_to: All California employers
rules.verbatim_quote: Regulatory, General and Serious -- the Proposed Penalty is multiplied by five. However, the penalty for any willful violation shall not be less than $11,632 and shall not exceed $162,851.
rules.notes: Regulatory/general maximum and repeat/willful caps are inflation-adjusted each January 1 (last amendment shown on DIR page: filed 12-19-2024, operative 1-1-2025). Check for a 2026 adjustment before using as a hard cap.

rules.title: No IIPP = serious-violation penalties not reduced (except size)
rules.plain_english: If you do not have an operative IIPP, Cal/OSHA will not reduce penalties for serious violations for good faith or history, only for business size.
rules.applies_to: All California employers
rules.verbatim_quote: (8) Injury Prevention Program -- The penalty for any Serious violation shall not be subject to adjustment pursuant to this subsection other than for Size as set forth in part (1) of this subsection where the employer does not have an operative injury prevention program

rules.title: Submit abatement statement within 10 working days to keep 50% credit
rules.plain_english: To get the 50% abatement credit on a serious violation not abated during the inspection, submit a statement signed under penalty of perjury (with evidence) within 10 working days after the abatement period ends. Missing it rescinds the credit and adds failure-to-abate penalties.

parameters.trigger: end of abatement period fixed in citation

rules.applies_to: Cited employers
rules.verbatim_quote: The signed statement and supporting evidence must be received within 10 working days after the end of the period fixed in the citation for abatement.

rules.title: New employers: 1-year grace for IIPP regulatory/general penalties
rules.plain_english: No civil penalty is assessed against a new employer for a regulatory or general IIPP violation during its first year in California if it made a good-faith effort to comply. Employers who adopt and implement Cal/OSHA's Model IIPP for non-high-hazard employment get no penalty for a first IIPP violation.
rules.applies_to: New employers establishing a business in California
rules.verbatim_quote: (10) No civil penalty shall be assessed against any new employer for a period of one year after the date the new employer establishes a business in the state for a regulatory or general violation of the Injury and Illness Prevention Program Standard
rules.notes: Construction is generally high-hazard, so the non-high-hazard model-program safe harbor may not apply.

rules.title: CSLB discipline for safety violations (B&P 7109.5)
rules.plain_english: A CSLB licensee can be disciplined for violating tree-work safety orders (8 CCR 3420 et seq.) regardless of injury, or any Labor Code Division 5 (Cal/OSHA) safety provision that results in death or serious injury to an employee. CSLB citation civil penalty range for 7109.5: $500 to $8,000.

parameters.trigger_death_or_serious_injury: any Labor Code Division 5 safety provision

rules.applies_to: CSLB licensees
rules.source_location: PDF page 351 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book; PDF page 540 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.verbatim_quote: (b) Violation of any safety provision in, or authorized by, Division 5 (commencing with Section 6300) of the Labor Code resulting in death or serious injury to an employee constitutes a cause for disciplinary action.
rules.notes: B&P 7110(c): willful/deliberate violation of safety laws is also cause for discipline (CCR 884 range $200-$30,000).

rules.title: Criminal liability: willful violation causing death or prolonged impairment
rules.plain_english: Employers, and anyone directing or controlling employees, who willfully violate a safety standard causing an employee's death or prolonged bodily impairment can be fined and/or imprisoned on conviction.

elements: causes death or prolonged impairment of employee
who: employee having direction, management control, or custody of employment

rules.applies_to: Employers and supervisors
rules.source_location: PDF page 49 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.verbatim_quote: who willfully violates any occupational safety or health standard that causes the death of any employee or the prolonged impairment of the body of any employee shall, upon conviction, be punished by a fine and or imprisonment
rules.notes: Specific fine/prison amounts are in Labor Code 6425 (leginfo not reachable); the Law Book does not state them.
